distance_note: On Terry A. Francois Blvd, within the stretch DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary marks as Mission Bay South, and about 30m from Mission Bay South's own nearest tracked feature (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 waterfront lawn) -- versus roughly 470m from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50). Recorded as adjacent to Mission Bay, not Mission Rock, on that basis. Pier 54 itself predates and is not part of Mission Bay's OCII development program -- it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure.
summary: Pier 54, a Port-owned pier on Terry A. Francois Blvd, was red-tagged in early July 2024, according to SFGate. In an August 2024 memo, Port Engineering recommended closing it to the public and tenants for safety reasons, and the 11 tenants were told to vacate by the end of 2024. The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) proposes $2.0M to demolish the pier's shed; that is a proposed budget line, and no source read says demolition has started or gives a start date.

milestones.text: Pier 54 is officially red-tagged, which SFGate (September 2024) describes as deteriorating with no viable restoration plans.

Port sends Pier 54's tenants formal written notice of the pier's closure; its August 9, 2024 memo says the 11 tenants will need to vacate by the end of 2024 (a planned date, written before it arrived). SFGate reported in September 2024 that the pier would permanently close at the end of the year.

At the Port Commission's February 25, 2025 meeting, a member of the public said in comment that Pier 54 "has recently been vacated of the businesses occupying it"; the minutes record the statement, which is not a Port finding.

A Port memo to the Commission on the FY2026-27 and 2027-28 budget refers to "the Pier 54 shed closure" as a factor constraining revenues, and lists the "Pier 54 Shed Demolition" among sample projects.

Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) proposes a "Pier 54 Shed Demolition" line item totaling $2.0M: $500,000 in FY2026-27 and $1,500,000 in FY2027-28. It is a proposed budget line for the shed only; no line item for full substructure removal appears in the same document, and no source read says the demolition has started.

Shed demolition is budgeted in the draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program for FY2026-27 and FY2027-28 (July 2026 to June 2028). This is a proposed budget line, not a start date: no source read gives a demolition date, and the draft's adoption is not confirmed.

open_questions: No funded plan yet for removing the pier's substructure beyond the shed demolition.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the closure-announcement milestone was dated December 2024, but the Port's August 9, 2024 memo says formal written notice went to tenants on July 15, 2024 and SFGate reported the closure in September 2024; it is now dated July 15, 2024. The February 2026 draft CIP milestone was flagged expected although the draft was published then; the flag was removed. Corrected 2026-10-12: the map status was 'being removed' and the summary said the pier was 'condemned and closed in 2024'. No source read says removal has begun, and 'condemned' appears in none of them (they say 'red tagged' and close 'for safety reasons'). The status is now 'existing', and the shed demolition appears as an expected milestone from the draft budget line.

Whether the pier closed and its tenants left on the planned end-of-2024 date is not stated by a Port document read. The August 2024 memo and the September 2024 SFGate article were written before that date; the later sources found are a February 2025 public comment that the pier "has recently been vacated" and a February 2026 Port memo that mentions "the Pier 54 shed closure".
Whether the Port adopted the FY2027-31 Five-Year Capital Improvement Program with the Pier 54 shed demolition line unchanged is not confirmed: the document read is a draft (cover: February 2026).

That the Port planned to fence the pier to prevent vandalism is reported only in a search-engine summary of the SFGate article, not independently re-verified here against the full original article text (which sits behind a paywall; the mirror used for this record's other facts may not repeat that detail).

This record's site grouping ("Mission Bay South") reflects DataSF's official redevelopment-project-area boundary, which reaches this stretch of Terry A. Francois Blvd -- not a claim that Pier 54 is a Mission Bay OCII development block, which it is not.
